sources.title: John Milnor, Link Groups
sources.locator: Complete 20-page paper, §§1–7, printed pp. 177–195 (PDF pp. 1–20). The local claims below are convention checks and scope comparisons; the batch supplies its own proofs.

contents.name: §2 Basic theorems: link group, homotopy invariance, meridian and parallel pairs
contents.reason: Actualsource conventions cross-checked by owner; full local coefficient-ideal/peripheral-kernel/selfcrossing proof now supplied and independently read by root. No source citation stands in for its proof.

contents.name: §2 Lemma 4: meridians normally generate the deleted-component kernel
contents.reason: The component-meridian generation result is proved locally from exterior H1 and lower-central commutator weights; Milnor’s normal-generation lemma is a convention and context check.

contents.name: §3 Theorem 4 and its parallel-link example
contents.reason: This section treats a special triviality criterion for links built from parallel components; that separate criterion is outside the finite Milnor coefficient and peripheral quotient scope of this pair.

contents.name: §4 Trivial links: group-ring word problem and decision procedure
contents.reason: The word-problem procedure for trivial links is not required for the local finite Magnus expansion or the bounded based-diagram algorithm authored here.

contents.name: §5 Almost trivial links: higher linking coefficients and the three-component example
contents.reason: The Borromean coefficient is recomputed from the declared braid diagram and finite Magnus multiplication; the source example is a comparison check only.

contents.name: §6 Arbitrary links in Euclidean space: link-group presentation and residue indeterminacy
contents.reason: The local definition states its finite based lifts and gcd convention explicitly; the source’s residue discussion is used to compare conventions, not to prove lift independence.

contents.name: §7 Arbitrary manifolds: link structures over nontrivial ambient fundamental groups
contents.reason: The assigned pages concern classical labeled links in S3 and based string links in a cylinder; ambient-manifold generalizations are explicitly outside this scope.

sources.title: John McCleary, Nontrivial fundamental groups
sources.locator: §8bis.2, Theorem 8bis.12 and its construction, Theorem 8bis.14 and proof, Proposition 8bis.13, and Theorem 8bis.16 with its full induction; PDF pp. 11–15.

contents.name: Theorem 8bis.12: homological Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence
contents.reason: The A-page supplier gives a separate classifying-space and Serre-fibration proof, with its full-AC and dependent-choice branch declared.

contents.name: Theorem 8bis.14: five-term exact sequence of a group extension
contents.reason: The local proof identifies H0(Q;H1(N)) with N/[G,N] and tracks the transgression.

contents.name: Proposition 8bis.13: finite normal Sylow subgroup application
contents.reason: This finite-group application is unrelated to the integral lower-central quotient induction required by KT-53.

contents.name: Theorem 8bis.16: H1-isomorphism and H2-epimorphism imply finite lower-central isomorphisms
contents.reason: The local proof reproduces the extension five-term diagram, cokernel identification, and elementwise middle-group lift argument.

sources.title: Stefan Friedl, Knot Theory
sources.locator: §5.1, Theorems 5.1–5.2 (printed pp. 64–65); §5.3, complete proof of Proposition 5.5 and Lemma 5.6 (printed pp. 69–73); §7.1, longitude definition, Sputnik Lemma 7.1, Lemma 7.2 and trefoil example (printed pp. 95–97).

contents.name: Theorem 5.1: HNN gluing across a two-sided codimension-one submanifold
contents.reason: Friedl states the general gluing theorem with a proof citation; the batch proves the simply connected case locally from an explicit connected-overlap Seifert–van Kampen cover.

contents.name: Theorem 5.2: bicollar neighborhood for a proper codimension-one submanifold
contents.reason: The upper-region proof instead supplies a tubular neighborhood for its proper sheets and checks the two side components and their retractions.

contents.name: Claim 2 in Proposition 5.5 proof: upper-region free meridian basis
contents.reason: The local upper-region proof defines the vertical sheets and proves freeness by successive cut-and-glue steps.

contents.name: Claim 3 and final step in Proposition 5.5 proof: puncture circles give Wirtinger relators
contents.reason: The local item uses only the normal closure, so conjugacy or inversion of a based puncture circle does not change the presentation.

contents.name: Proposition 5.5: Wirtinger presentation and omission of any one relator
contents.reason: The local proof retains the source/target convention and proves relator omission from the punctured-sphere normal-generation lemma.

sources.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
sources.locator: Complete book PDF, §1.3 on covering spaces and homotopy lifting, and §2.2, Theorem 2.35 on cellular homology and naturality; the chapter’s stated coverage does not include a Serre spectral-sequence proof.

contents.name: §1.3: covering-space classification and homotopy lifting
contents.reason: The local classifying-map arguments use explicit CW extension and mapping-path constructions; no covering-classification theorem is needed for the KT-53 group-homology branch.

sources.title: Wolfram MathWorld, Borromean Rings
sources.locator: Complete article entry on the standard three-braid closure and pairwise unlinking; used only as a notation and identification check.

contents.name: Standard Borromean braid closure and pairwise unlinking
contents.reason: The braid convention is checked against the displayed local diagram; all six crossing labels, pairwise linking sums, and the Magnus coefficient are verified in the example itself.

alternatives.argument: The finite coefficient definition is stated explicitly and cross-checked against the complete 1954 Link Groups paper §§5–6 and Stees §2.5; the local item declares arbitrary finite closed-link lift choices rather than claiming their invariance.

The local proof expands the conjugation in the completed noncommutative series ring and enumerates the finite degree-m word decompositions; this coefficient argument does not rely on an unread source passage.

Current full proof: finite target-subsequence ring annihilates exact peripheral-kernel relators; basis-conjugating substitution and triangular lower-coefficient induction prove equal moduli for arbitrary basings/lifts. Reduced crossing presentations and normalized longitudes yield distinct-index selfcrossing invariance. Final R1augmentation explicitly covers underpass-free components.

Current three-step proof transports peripheral data under isotopy and applies proved basing/lift independence, then composes the proved distinct-index selfcrossing equalities. Stringlink branch uses actual nilpotent end isomorphisms.

Finite truncated ring arithmetic and degree-stability are specified locally; actual link peripheral words and positive Wirtinger presentation are now proved suppliers. The algorithm returns specified based coefficients; invariance is supplied by the separately completed theorem, not unread1957 text.
The six-crossing table, pairwise linking scan and truncated Magnus multiplication are verified directly from the declared braid diagram; the source is not used as a proof.
